purpose: Establish whether openappindex.org is present in Perplexity's retrieval set. This is a PRECONDITION probe, not a gate scoring run: the query is deliberately NOT one of the 18 frozen protocol queries, so the scored set stays uncontaminated.
session: logged-in (free plan; 'Kostenlose Vorschau der erweiterten Suche' active)
retrieval_note: UI reported 'Gesucht, Inhalt abgerufen' (searched, content fetched) after 5s.

figures_attributed_to_us.recall: 81% / 579 von 715  -- CURRENT, matches the served index
figures_attributed_to_us.free_listed_but_charging: 706 von 916  -- SUPERSEDED. The served index has published 697 of 907 since 2026-08-31.

staleness_finding: The free-listed-but-charging figure Perplexity attributes to us is the pre-correction basis, superseded by the 2026-08-31 amendment (ten press products removed; 951 -> 941 apps). Both README.md and the landing page carried 706 of 916 until commit 573263c on 2026-08-31; neither does now. No live page serves that pair today. Perplexity's copy therefore predates 2026-08-31 by at least 23 days.
significance: The homepage is in Perplexity's retrieval set although Google has excluded it as noindex since 22 August -- Perplexity's own crawler reached what Google's index does not hold.
A question page (one of the four) was retrieved, not only the root.
Being cited is not the same as being cited CURRENTLY: an index that publishes dated corrections has no mechanism to retract a superseded figure from an assistant's cache.
what_this_is_not: Not a gate score. The entity-style probe used here is the easiest possible case and group D (entity lookups) was de-weighted on 2026-08-23 precisely because assistants already handle it. Whether Perplexity cites the index for the 15 scored, generic queries is unmeasured and remains the experiment.
